**Visual Analysis:**
- Young corn seedling (~V3-V5 stage) lying completely flat on bare soil
- Plant has fully collapsed/lodged — not just wilted
- Base/lower stalk area appears dark and rotted
- Leaves still largely green, suggesting sudden collapse rather than gradual die-off
- No leaf lesions, spots, or foliar disease patterns visible

**Reasoning:**
The image shows a classic lodged/collapsed young corn plant with what appears to be base rot. The sudden collapse of an otherwise green plant with dark, rotted tissue at the stalk base is the hallmark of **Bacterial stalk rot** (*Erwinia*), which causes rapid water-soaking and maceration of lower internodes, leading to plant collapse. The reference images confirm this pattern — plants falling over due to stalk base rot, with otherwise green tissue above the infection point.
